newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Hard Rock Cafe faces closure on banned beef.
newsitem.headline: Paris Hard Rock Cafe faces closure on banned beef.

text.p: The Paris police chief said on Friday he had started legal proceedings to close down the French capital's Hard Rock Cafe over suspicion of having used British beef, banned over fears of mad cow disease.
The restaurant, which says the meat came legally from Irish cows, has four days to present its defence in writing.
Police said health inspectors on a routine check found 300 kg (660 lbs) of frozen hamburgers bearing stamps indicating an English origin at the restaurant on the Boulevard Montmartre.

The Hard Rock Cafe, one of an American-style chain owned by the Rank Organisation, said it had certificates to prove the meat was from cows bred, raised and slaughtered in Ireland, and therefore conformed to French law.
It said the confusion arose because the meat had passed through a processing centre in Britain, one which dealt exclusively with Irish products and had "all necessary permits to export to Europe".

France led a worldwide ban on imports of British beef in March over fears that mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could be passed to humans. BSE is most widespread in Britain.
